questions.stem: An economy's real GDP is above its trend level, but the gap is narrowing. The unemployment rate is still falling and incomes are still growing. The economy is most likely in:

choices.C: a contraction

questions.explanation: Fix both coordinates: ABOVE trend + gap FALLING = slowdown. Expansion is above trend and rising; contraction is below trend and falling. 'Unemployment still falling, incomes still growing' is exactly the slowdown row of the Exhibit 1 grid — the labor market lags, so it tempts you toward 'expansion'.
questions.kr: 두 좌표를 고정: 추세 위 + 격차 축소 = 둔화(slowdown). 확장은 추세 위+상승, 수축은 추세 아래+하락. '실업률은 여전히 하락'은 노동시장이 후행하기 때문 — 확장으로 유도하는 함정.

questions.stem: Which spending category most likely gives the earliest signal of a general cyclical recovery?

choices.C: Durable goods

questions.explanation: Durables are postponable (long useful life), so households resume deferred purchases first when the outlook improves — a pickup in durables is the curriculum's early signal of a broader recovery, and weakness in durables is the early sign of a downturn. Non-durables barely change through the cycle; services sit between.
questions.kr: 내구재는 미룰 수 있는 소비(긴 사용수명) → 전망이 좋아지면 가장 먼저 반등 → 회복의 조기 신호. 비내구재는 거의 변화 없음, 서비스는 중간.

questions.stem: Spending on non-durable goods shows little change through the business cycle most likely because:

choices.A: non-durables are purchased out of permanent income
choices.C: they have a shorter useful life than services

questions.explanation: Cyclicality runs through deferrability. Food and medicine are used up and must be re-bought in every phase — replacement cannot be postponed — so demand is stable. Choice A mixes in the income mapping (permanent income → services); choice C compares with services, which is irrelevant to the mechanism.
questions.kr: 경기순응성 = 연기 가능성. 식품·의약품은 소모되어 매 국면 다시 사야 함 → 미룰 수 없음 → 수요 안정. A는 소득 매핑 혼동, C는 무관한 비교.

questions.stem: As an economic expansion matures, the first sign of a cyclical downturn in the housing sector is most likely:

choices.A: a decline in residential construction activity
choices.C: a fall in household incomes

questions.explanation: Sequence: prices and mortgage rates rise disproportionately → affordability worsens EVEN AS incomes rise → house SALES slow (first) → unsold inventory builds (second) → construction turns down (last). Incomes are still rising at this point, so C is wrong; construction is the last step, so A is wrong.
questions.kr: 순서: 가격·금리 과도 상승 → 소득이 늘어도 구입 부담 ↑ → 판매 둔화(1) → 미판매 재고 누적(2) → 건설 감소(3). 소득은 아직 상승 중(C 오답), 건설은 마지막(A 오답).

questions.stem: A more severe housing-market correction is most likely the result of:

choices.B: late buying by households seeking exposure to expected price gains
choices.C: rising mortgage rates during the recovery phase

questions.explanation: Late buying for expected gains extends the upswing and invites overbuilding → large unsold inventory → downward price pressure → catches stretched late buyers → more severe correction (the 2008–09 pattern). Demographics are a trend, not a cycle driver; rising rates slow buying but are not what makes the correction severe.
questions.kr: 기대 차익을 노린 후기 매수 → 상승 연장 → 과잉건설 → 미판매 재고 → 가격 압력 → 무리한 후기 매수자 타격 → 더 심한 조정(2008–09). 인구는 추세 요인, 금리 상승은 조정의 '심각성' 원인이 아님.

questions.stem: An analyst compares three domestic companies: a restaurant chain, a maker of industrial machinery sold to local manufacturers, and a supermarket operator. Ranked from most to least sensitive to the domestic business cycle, the order is most likely:

choices.C: machinery, supermarkets, restaurants

questions.explanation: Translate each company into a GDP component first: machinery sold to manufacturers = business investment (I) — most cyclical; restaurants = services (middle); supermarkets = non-durables (least). Full ranking: I > durables > services > non-durables. Business I is the top rung — don't truncate it.
questions.kr: 기업을 GDP 구성요소로 먼저 번역: 기계(기업 투자 I) > 식당(서비스) > 슈퍼마켓(비내구재). 전체 순위 I > 내구재 > 서비스 > 비내구재 — I가 맨 위.

questions.stem: Which is most likely to reduce a country's net exports significantly?

choices.A: A sharp one-quarter depreciation of its currency
choices.B: A multi-year cumulative appreciation of its currency
choices.C: A multi-year cumulative depreciation of its currency

questions.explanation: Two tests: direction and persistence. Appreciation makes exports pricier abroad and imports cheaper → net exports ↓ (depreciation does the opposite, so C is wrong). And currency moves affect trade only when they cumulate in one direction for some time — a one-quarter move, however sharp, has minimal effect (so A is wrong).
questions.kr: 방향 + 지속성 두 가지 검사. 통화 강세 → 수출 비싸짐·수입 저렴 → 순수출 ↓ (약세는 반대, C 오답). 환율은 한 방향으로 누적될 때만 무역에 영향 — 한 분기 급변동은 효과 미미(A 오답).

questions.stem: Working-age population 50m; employed 30m; unemployed 2m; 1m discouraged workers. The unemployment rate and participation rate are closest to:
questions.explanation: Discouraged workers are OUTSIDE the labor force. Labor force = 30 + 2 = 32m. Unemployment rate = 2/32 = 6.25%. Participation rate = 32/50 = 64%. Choice B/C add the 1m discouraged to the labor force (33m → 66%); C also divides by 33 (6.06%).
questions.kr: 실망 실업자는 경제활동인구 밖. 경제활동인구 = 30+2 = 32m. 실업률 = 2/32 = 6.25%, 참가율 = 32/50 = 64%. B·C는 실망 실업자 1m을 잘못 포함(33m).

questions.stem: A full-time engineer takes a part-time retail job after a layoff and continues to seek engineering work. For the official unemployment rate she is most likely counted as:

choices.C: outside the labor force

questions.explanation: She has a job, so she is EMPLOYED — she is underemployed (overqualified / part-time wanting full-time), which is 'hidden unemployment' and does not appear in the official rate. Still seeking work does not make an employed person 'unemployed'; discouraged workers (stopped looking) are the ones outside the labor force.
questions.kr: 일자리가 있으므로 '취업자'. 불완전고용(과잉자격/파트타임)은 숨은 실업 — 공식 실업률에 안 잡힘. 구직 중이어도 취업자는 실업자가 아니고, 경제활동인구 밖은 '실망 실업자'(구직 포기).

questions.stem: The unemployment rate remains high, but overtime hours and output per hour worked have both started to rise, while full-time payrolls are flat. The labor market is most likely signaling:

choices.C: the peak of the cycle

questions.explanation: The discriminator is hours and productivity, not the (lagging) unemployment rate. Rising overtime + rising productivity with hiring not yet restarted = firms working retained staff harder before committing to full-time hires = END of recession. A deepening recession shows hours and productivity falling; a peak shows low unemployment and high hours.
questions.kr: 판별 기준은 (후행하는) 실업률이 아니라 근로시간·생산성. 초과근무↑ + 생산성↑ + 아직 채용 없음 = 보유 인력을 먼저 더 쓰는 단계 = 경기침체 종료. 침체 심화는 시간·생산성 하락, 정점은 낮은 실업률·긴 근로시간.

questions.stem: Base-period basket: 20 loaves of bread at 1.50 and 10 liters of milk at 2.00. Current prices: bread 1.80, milk 2.10; current quantities: 25 loaves, 8 liters. The Laspeyres inflation rate is closest to:
questions.explanation: Hold BASE quantities fixed and apply current prices. Base cost = 20×1.50 + 10×2.00 = 50.0. Same basket at current prices = 20×1.80 + 10×2.10 = 57.0. Index = 57/50 × 100 = 114.0 → inflation = 14.0%. Choice B (15.5%) uses CURRENT quantities in both periods (61.8/53.5 — a Paasche-style number, the GDP-deflator convention); choice C averages the two price changes (20% and 5%) without weights. Read which quantities are held fixed.

questions.stem: An analyst wants to track the trend in an airline's fuel and labor costs. The most appropriate data source is:

choices.A: the CPI sub-index for air travel
choices.B: the PPI/WPI sub-indexes for fuel and the relevant wage-cost indicators
choices.C: the headline CPI

questions.explanation: Costs = inputs = producer-side prices → PPI/WPI sub-indexes (plus wage-cost indicators for labor). The CPI sub-index for air travel measures the airline's OUTPUT (ticket) prices — the sales side, not costs. Headline CPI is an economy-wide consumer measure, irrelevant to one industry's inputs.
questions.kr: 비용 = 투입물 = 생산자 가격 → PPI/WPI 하위지수(+임금비용 지표). 항공요금 CPI 하위지수는 산출(판매) 가격. 헤드라인 CPI는 경제 전체 소비자 물가로 무관.

questions.stem: The 10-year nominal government bond yields 4.2% and the 10-year inflation-linked bond yields 1.7%. The market-implied average annual inflation over 10 years is closest to:
questions.explanation: Breakeven inflation ≈ nominal yield − inflation-linked (real) yield = 4.2% − 1.7% = 2.5%. Choice A is the real yield itself; choice C adds the two. Caveat the curriculum quotes: the inflation-linked market is small, so pension-fund demand can distort the reading.
questions.kr: 기대 인플레이션(breakeven) ≈ 명목 수익률 − 물가연동채 수익률 = 4.2 − 1.7 = 2.5%. A는 실질 수익률, C는 합산 오류. 시장이 작아 연기금 수요가 왜곡할 수 있다는 주의 문구.

questions.stem: The velocity of money has fallen because the central bank sharply expanded the money supply while nominal GDP was unchanged. An analyst should most likely conclude that:

choices.C: disinflation is likely

questions.explanation: Velocity = nominal GDP / money supply. It fell because the DENOMINATOR (money) rose → more money relative to output → inflationary pressure. Had it fallen because GDP (numerator) dropped in a cyclical correction, a cyclical upswing would be the reading (A). Rising velocity signals a money shortage → disinflation (C). 'Velocity fell' alone is never enough — ask which side moved.
questions.kr: 유통속도 = 명목GDP / 통화량. 분모(통화) 증가로 하락 → 산출 대비 돈이 많음 → 인플레이션 압력. 분자(GDP) 감소로 하락했다면 경기 반등 신호(A). 유통속도 상승 = 통화 부족 → 디스인플레이션(C). 어느 쪽이 움직였는지 반드시 확인.

questions.stem: A country's core CPI is constructed from the same fixed basket as its headline CPI, minus food and energy. Compared with headline, core inflation most likely:

choices.B: has the same upward bias but less short-term volatility
choices.C: has no upward bias

questions.explanation: Upward bias (substitution, quality, new-product) comes from index CONSTRUCTION — the fixed basket — and applies to any Laspeyres index, headline or core alike. Excluding food and energy is a COMPOSITION choice that removes short-term noise, not bias. Two separate concepts: bias = methodology; volatility = composition.
questions.kr: 상향 편의(대체·품질·신제품)는 고정 바스켓이라는 '구성 방법'에서 나오므로 헤드라인·근원 모두 동일. 식품·에너지 제외는 '구성 품목' 선택 → 단기 변동성만 줄임. 편의 = 방법론, 변동성 = 구성.

questions.stem: Spending on durable goods shows the most pronounced cyclical swings most likely because durable goods:

choices.A: have a long useful life, so their replacement can be deferred
choices.B: are purchases that cannot be postponed
choices.C: are more essential to households than non-durables and services

questions.explanation: Mechanism: long useful life → replacement can be deferred (repair instead) → purchases postponed in downturns and resumed in recoveries → most cyclical. Test any 'because' option: would it make demand MORE or LESS stable? Necessity (choice C) would make demand stable, like food — the opposite of cyclicality. Choice B is the exact reverse of the mechanism.
questions.kr: 긴 사용수명 → 교체를 미룰 수 있음(수리로 버팀) → 불황에 구매 연기, 회복에 재개 → 가장 경기순응적. '필수적이라서'(C)는 수요를 안정시키는 이유 — 경기순응성과 반대. B는 메커니즘의 정반대.

questions.stem: The concept of permanent income is most useful for predicting a household's:

choices.C: spending on durable goods

questions.explanation: Three-way mapping: permanent income → basic/discretionary consumption including SERVICES; disposable income (any source, windfalls included) → DURABLES; short-term uncertainty (precautionary motive) → SAVING RATE. Three behaviors, three different drivers — the exam pairs them wrong.
questions.kr: 3방향 매핑: 항상소득 → 기본·재량 소비(서비스 포함); 가처분소득(출처 무관) → 내구재; 단기 불확실성(예비적 동기) → 저축률. 세 행동, 세 다른 원인.

questions.stem: A country's imports most clearly respond to:

choices.A: the same factors that drive its exports
choices.C: its domestic GDP growth rate

questions.explanation: The Exhibit 2 asymmetry: imports follow the DOMESTIC cycle (they are domestic demand for foreign goods); exports follow FOREIGN cycles. 'Industrial policy' appears nowhere in the curriculum's model — a plausible-sounding off-model option. Write the rule's right-hand side ('domestic GDP growth') before reading the options.
questions.kr: Exhibit 2 비대칭: 수입 ← 국내 경기(해외 재화에 대한 국내 수요), 수출 ← 해외 경기. '산업정책'은 교재 모형에 없는 선지. 선지를 읽기 전에 규칙의 우변('국내 GDP 성장')을 먼저 쓴다.

questions.stem: A portfolio manager reviews three domestic companies: one sells consumer electronics and small vehicles locally; one sells production equipment to domestic companies; one sells household and personal-care products at home and abroad. Which company's sales most likely fluctuate the most with the domestic business cycle?

choices.A: The consumer electronics and vehicles company
choices.C: The household and personal-care products company

questions.explanation: Translate into GDP components, then rank: equipment sold to companies = business investment (I) = MOST cyclical; electronics/vehicles = consumer durables (2nd); household/personal care = non-durables (least, and partly export-driven, so even less tied to the domestic cycle). The ranking is I > durables > services > non-durables — I is not optional.
questions.kr: GDP 구성요소로 번역 후 순위: 기업용 설비 = 기업 투자(I) = 가장 경기순응적; 전자·차량 = 소비 내구재(2위); 생활용품 = 비내구재(최하, 일부 수출이라 국내 경기와 더 멀다). I > 내구재 > 서비스 > 비내구재.

questions.stem: In an inflationary environment, a price index built on a fixed basket of goods will, over time, most likely:

choices.A: overstate the true cost of living
choices.B: understate the true cost of living
choices.C: track the true cost of living quite closely

questions.explanation: 'Fixed basket' is the trigger word: fixed basket = Laspeyres = three biases (substitution, quality, new-product) — ALL upward → overstates inflation and the cost of living. Three upward biases cannot net to 'tracks closely'.
questions.kr: '고정 바스켓'이 트리거: 고정 바스켓 = 라스파이레스 = 세 가지 편의(대체·품질·신제품) 모두 상향 → 과대평가. 세 상향 편의가 '정확히 추적'으로 상쇄될 수 없다.

questions.stem: To estimate trends in both the sales and the production costs of a particular industry, an analyst would most appropriately use:

choices.A: sub-indexes of the wholesale/producer price index only
choices.B: sub-indexes of both the consumer price index and the wholesale/producer price index
choices.C: the headline consumer price index

questions.explanation: Sales/output prices → CPI sub-index (market prices of the industry's products, including markups). Production costs/input prices → WPI/PPI sub-index. The stem names TWO objects (sales AND costs), so the option must cover two. A WPI sub-index alone misses the output side and may not reflect markups.
questions.kr: 판매(산출 가격) → CPI 하위지수(마크업 포함 시장가격); 생산비용(투입 가격) → WPI/PPI 하위지수. 지문이 두 대상(판매 AND 비용)을 묻으면 선지도 두 개를 덮어야 한다.

questions.concept: Headline vs. core — noise, not bias
questions.stem: Compared with core inflation, headline inflation most likely:

choices.B: is more subject to short-term market conditions
choices.C: is a more reliable predictor of future inflation

questions.explanation: Headline includes food and energy, which swing with short-term supply/demand conditions that may not persist → noisier, and NOT a reliable predictor (so C is wrong). Upward bias comes from index CONSTRUCTION (fixed basket) and applies equally to headline and core — composition does not add a bias. Bias = methodology; noise = composition.
questions.kr: 헤드라인은 식품·에너지를 포함 → 단기 수급 변동에 민감 → 노이즈가 크고 예측력이 낮음(C 오답). 상향 편의는 지수 '구성 방법'(고정 바스켓)에서 나와 헤드라인·근원에 동일 적용. 편의 = 방법론, 노이즈 = 구성.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a limitation of the natural rate of unemployment (NARU/NAIRU) concept?

choices.A: It is only valid within monetarist models of the economy
choices.B: It changes over time as technology and economic structure change
choices.C: An economy-wide rate can miss bottlenecks in particular labor-market segments

questions.explanation: NOT routine: mark each option T/F, then pick the F. B is TRUE (NAIRU varies across economies and over time) and C is TRUE (aggregate NAIRU misses segment bottlenecks such as tech workers) — both are real limitations and therefore distractors here. A is FALSE: NAIRU is a labor-market concept that belongs to no school of macro models. In a NOT question, 'sounds right' is the trap.
questions.kr: NOT 루틴: 선지마다 T/F 표시 후 F를 고른다. B(시간에 따라 변함)·C(부문별 병목 놓침)는 교재에 있는 진짜 한계 → NOT 문제에선 오답. A는 거짓: NAIRU는 어느 학파 모형에도 속하지 않는 노동시장 개념.

questions.stem: To examine inflationary pressure arising from rising costs, an analyst would most appropriately gather data on:

choices.A: money supply growth and nominal GDP growth
choices.B: the unemployment rate relative to NAIRU, and wage growth relative to productivity growth
choices.C: capacity utilization and the gap between actual and potential GDP

questions.explanation: Label the type first: 'rising costs' = COST-PUSH → labor-market data (UR vs NAIRU; wages vs productivity → ULC). Money vs nominal GDP (A) and capacity/potential GDP (C) are DEMAND-PULL indicators. The stem names the type; the type picks the row of the indicator map.
questions.kr: 유형부터 라벨링: '비용 상승' = 비용 인상(cost-push) → 노동시장 데이터(실업률 vs NAIRU, 임금 vs 생산성 → ULC). 통화 vs 명목GDP(A), 가동률·잠재GDP(C)는 수요 견인 지표.

questions.stem: Cost-push inflation is most likely to occur when the unemployment rate is:

choices.C: either high or low

questions.explanation: Unemployment below NAIRU → labor shortage → wages bid up → cost-push. Low unemployment = tight labor market = cost pressure; high unemployment = slack = no wage pressure. The mechanism is one-directional. Hedge options ('either / both / any') are distractors unless the curriculum literally says both apply.
questions.kr: 실업률이 NAIRU 아래 → 노동 부족 → 임금 상승 → 비용 인상 인플레이션. 낮은 실업률 = 타이트한 노동시장. 메커니즘은 한 방향. '둘 다/either' 식 선지는 교재가 명시적으로 둘 다라고 하지 않으면 오답.

questions.stem: According to monetarists, inflation is most likely:

choices.A: a reflection of the growth of the money supply
choices.B: driven by the level of interest rates
choices.C: caused by rising production costs

questions.explanation: Friedman: inflation is 'always and everywhere a monetary phenomenon' — too much money chasing too few goods. Monetarism is about the QUANTITY of money. Interest rates are a policy tool and part of AD transmission, but not the monetarist explanation; rising costs is cost-push. Adjacent concept ≠ stated concept.
questions.kr: 프리드먼: 인플레이션은 '언제 어디서나 화폐적 현상' — 통화량 증가. 금리는 정책 수단일 뿐 통화주의 설명이 아님, 비용 상승은 cost-push. 인접 개념 ≠ 교재가 말한 개념.

questions.stem: During a deepening recession, a large number of unemployed workers stop looking for work. Holding everything else constant, the reported unemployment rate and the participation rate will most likely:

choices.C: the unemployment rate rises and the participation rate falls

questions.explanation: Discouraged workers leave the labor force: the numerator (unemployed) and the denominator (labor force) of the unemployment rate both fall by the same amount, which lowers the ratio (e.g., 5/65 = 7.69% → 4/64 = 6.25%). The participation rate (LF / working-age pop) also falls. Rule: UR ↓ with PR ↓ = people giving up, not improvement — always read UR with PR.
questions.kr: 실망 실업자가 경제활동인구에서 빠지면 실업률의 분자·분모가 같은 양만큼 줄어 비율 하락(5/65 = 7.69% → 4/64 = 6.25%). 참가율도 하락. 실업률↓ + 참가율↓ = 구직 포기, 개선 아님 — 항상 두 지표를 함께 본다.

questions.stem: A country's inflation rate falls from 8% to 3% over two years. This is best described as:

choices.C: stagflation

questions.explanation: Disinflation = a decline in the inflation RATE while it stays positive — the price level is still rising, just more slowly. Deflation requires a negative rate (falling price level). Stagflation needs a second variable (high unemployment / slow growth) and cannot be identified from the inflation rate alone.
questions.kr: 디스인플레이션 = 인플레이션율이 하락하지만 양(+)으로 유지 — 물가는 여전히 오르는 중. 디플레이션은 음(−)의 상승률. 스태그플레이션은 실업·성장이라는 두 번째 변수가 필요해 인플레이션율만으로는 식별 불가.

questions.stem: Base period: 50 kg of rice at 3.0 and 70 liters of gasoline at 4.4. Current period: 70 kg of rice at 4.0 and 60 liters of gasoline at 4.5. The current-period price index (base = 100) is closest to:
questions.explanation: Laspeyres: hold BASE quantities (50, 70) fixed. Base cost = 50×3.0 + 70×4.4 = 458. Same basket at current prices = 50×4.0 + 70×4.5 = 515. Index = 515/458 × 100 = 112.45 → inflation 12.45%. Choice B (≈116.0) uses current quantities in both periods (a Paasche-style number); the GDP deflator is the reverse convention — don't cross them.
questions.kr: 라스파이레스: 기준기 수량(50, 70) 고정. 기준 비용 458, 현재 가격 적용 515 → 지수 112.45 → 인플레이션 12.45%. B(≈116)는 현재 수량을 양 기간에 쓴 값(파셰). GDP 디플레이터는 반대 관례.

questions.stem: The velocity of money declines because nominal GDP has dropped in a cyclical correction while the money supply is unchanged. The most likely implication is:

choices.C: a shortage of money threatens deflation

questions.explanation: Velocity = nominal GDP / money. Here the NUMERATOR fell in a cyclical correction — the ratio tends to restore itself, so a cyclical upswing is the reading, NOT inflation. Inflationary pressure is the reading when velocity falls because MONEY rose; a money shortage shows up as RISING velocity. Same direction, opposite conclusions — ask which side moved.
questions.kr: 유통속도 = 명목GDP / 통화. 분자(GDP)가 경기 조정으로 하락 → 비율이 복원되는 경기 반등 신호, 인플레이션 아님. 통화 증가로 하락했을 때가 인플레이션 압력; 통화 부족은 유통속도 '상승'으로 나타남.

questions.stem: The unemployment rate can keep rising even as an economic recovery gains momentum. This is most likely because:

choices.A: discouraged workers re-enter the labor force before they find jobs
choices.B: firms lay off workers aggressively at the start of a recovery
choices.C: productivity falls sharply as output recovers

questions.explanation: Two reasons unemployment lags: (1) the labor force expands with the economy — discouraged workers resume searching when prospects improve but seldom find work at once, pushing the rate up; (2) firms fully use retained workers (overtime, hours) before hiring. Layoffs at the start of a recovery (B) is backwards; productivity RISES early in a recovery (C is backwards).
questions.kr: 실업률이 후행하는 두 이유: (1) 경기 개선 시 실망 실업자가 구직 재개 → 바로 취업되지 않아 실업률 ↑; (2) 기업은 채용 전 보유 인력(초과근무)을 먼저 활용. 회복 초기 해고(B)는 반대, 생산성은 회복 초기에 상승(C 반대).

questions.stem: Hourly compensation rises 4.0% while output per hour rises 1.5%. Unit labor cost most likely changes by approximately:
questions.explanation: ULC = W / O (compensation per hour ÷ output per hour). In growth rates %ΔULC ≈ %ΔW − %ΔO = 4.0% − 1.5% = +2.5% → compensation is outrunning productivity → upward pressure on prices (cost-push signal). Choice B adds; choice C has the sign reversed.
questions.kr: ULC = W / O. 증가율로 %ΔULC ≈ %ΔW − %ΔO = 4.0 − 1.5 = +2.5% → 보수가 생산성을 앞질러 가격 상승 압력(비용 인상 신호). B는 합산, C는 부호 반대.

questions.stem: A country's domestic growth is slowing, yet its exports continue to grow strongly. The most likely explanation is that:

choices.A: its major trading partners are in a strong expansion
choices.B: its currency has appreciated sharply this quarter
choices.C: domestic demand for foreign goods has fallen

questions.explanation: Exports are driven by EXTERNAL demand (foreign cycles), so they can grow while the domestic economy slows if trading partners are strong — net trade may offset or even erase domestic weakness. A sharp appreciation would hurt exports (and a one-quarter move has little effect anyway); falling domestic demand for foreign goods describes imports, not exports.
questions.kr: 수출은 해외 수요(외국 경기)에 의해 결정 → 교역 상대국이 강하면 국내 둔화 중에도 수출 증가 가능; 순무역이 국내 약세를 상쇄·소거할 수 있다. 통화 강세는 수출에 불리(한 분기 변동은 효과 미미), 해외 재화에 대한 국내 수요는 수입의 이야기.

questions.stem: Household saving rates have risen sharply during a downturn, and the stock of accumulated savings is now unusually large. For the business cycle this most likely signals:

choices.A: near-term weakness in spending but greater longer-term capacity for recovery
choices.B: an immediate rebound in consumer spending
choices.C: sustained weakness with no recovery potential

questions.explanation: Two-sided signal: a RISING saving rate (flow) reflects caution and precautionary saving → near-term weakening; a large accumulated STOCK of savings → greater capacity to increase spending → longer-term recovery potential. Distractors present only one side.
questions.kr: 양면 신호: 저축률 상승(플로우) = 경계·예비적 저축 → 단기 약세; 누적 저축(스톡)이 크면 → 지출 여력 → 장기 회복 잠재력. 오답은 한쪽만 제시.

questions.stem: As an economy enters a downturn, which labor-market measure most likely deteriorates first?

choices.C: The unemployment rate

questions.explanation: Firms keep workers as output falls, so measured productivity (output/hours) drops first — before hours and overtime are cut, before temporary staff are released, and well before full-time layoffs. The unemployment rate is the LAGGING end of the chain: productivity → hours/overtime → temps → full-time payrolls → unemployment rate.
questions.kr: 산출이 줄어도 인력을 유지하므로 생산성(산출/시간)이 가장 먼저 하락 → 초과근무 축소 → 임시직 감축 → 정규직 해고 → 실업률(가장 후행). 순서: 생산성 → 시간 → 임시직 → 정규 급여 → 실업률.

questions.stem: Relative to its share of GDP, the housing sector's influence on overall economic fluctuations is most accurately described as:

choices.B: larger than its size suggests, because of its dramatic cyclical swings
choices.C: negligible, because it is a small sector

questions.explanation: Housing is a small part of the economy relative to consumer spending, but it experiences dramatic swings, so it counts more in overall economic movements than its size suggests — the same shape as business investment (small share, high volatility). In the US and UK property values also link to consumer wealth and confidence.
questions.kr: 주택은 GDP 비중은 작지만 변동이 매우 커서 규모 이상으로 경기 변동에 기여 — 기업 투자와 같은 구조(작은 비중, 높은 변동성). 미·영에서는 자산가치가 소비자 부(富)·신뢰와 연결.

questions.stem: To convert a country's nominal GDP growth into real growth, the most appropriate price measure is:

choices.C: the GDP deflator

questions.explanation: The GDP deflator reflects the prices of goods and services PRODUCED domestically — the output mix. CPI and PCE are built from CONSUMPTION baskets, which exclude exports, investment goods and government purchases and so can differ materially from output.
questions.kr: GDP 디플레이터는 국내에서 '생산된' 재화·서비스 가격(산출 구성). CPI·PCE는 '소비' 바스켓 기준 → 수출·투자재·정부구매가 빠져 산출과 차이.

questions.stem: The key to ending a hyperinflation is most likely:

choices.A: indexing wages and contracts to the price level
choices.B: regaining control of the money supply
choices.C: imposing price controls on essential goods

questions.explanation: Hyperinflation's basic cause is too much money in circulation — typically large-scale government spending not backed by taxes and accommodated by money printing. The cure follows from the cause: regain control of the money supply. Indexation entrenches the spiral; price controls do not address the cause.
questions.kr: 초인플레이션의 근본 원인은 과도한 통화 공급(세수 없는 재정지출 + 화폐 발행). 치료는 원인에서: 통화 공급 통제 회복. 물가연동은 악순환을 고착, 가격 통제는 원인 미해결.

questions.front: The four phases of Exhibit 1 — define each by BOTH coordinates (position vs trend, direction), and what employment does in each
questions.back:
Recovery: BELOW trend, RISING — unemployment above average, overtime before hiring, confidence starts improving.
Expansion: ABOVE trend, RISING — hiring restarts, unemployment stabilizes then falls.
Slowdown: ABOVE trend, FALLING — hiring slower but unemployment STILL falling, incomes still growing.
Contraction: BELOW trend, FALLING — cut overtime → freeze hiring → layoffs.
Peak/trough are turning points, not phases. Never classify by GDP direction alone.

questions.front: Cyclicality ranking of spending categories (all four rungs) and WHY durables are cyclical
questions.back:
Business investment (I) > Durables > Services > Non-durables.
Durables are cyclical because of LONG USEFUL LIFE → replacement deferrable (repair instead) → postponed in downturns. NOT because they are 'needed more' — necessity makes demand STABLE.
Scenario drill: 'equipment sold to companies' = I = most cyclical; electronics/vehicles = durables; food/personal care = non-durables. Translate companies into GDP components first.

questions.front: Permanent income, disposable income, short-term uncertainty — which behavior does each predict?
questions.back:
PERMANENT income → basic/discretionary consumption, incl. SERVICES.
DISPOSABLE income (regardless of source, windfalls included) → DURABLES.
Short-term UNCERTAINTY (precautionary motive) → SAVING RATE.
Saving rate: rate RISES = caution now (negative); large STOCK of savings = longer-term recovery capacity.

questions.front: Housing: the maturing-expansion sequence, and why late buying makes corrections worse
questions.back:
Prices & mortgage rates rise disproportionately → relative housing cost ↑ EVEN AS incomes rise → SALES slow (1st) → UNSOLD INVENTORY builds (2nd) → CONSTRUCTION turns down (3rd).
Late buying for expected gains extends the upswing → OVERBUILDING → inventory → price pressure → catches stretched late buyers → MORE SEVERE correction (2008–09).
Demographics (household formation, age 25–40) = TREND, 'little to do with business cycles'.

questions.front: What drives imports vs exports; the FX direction rule; when FX actually matters
questions.back:
IMPORTS ← DOMESTIC GDP growth (rise in expansion, PEAK in slowdown, fall below average in contraction).
EXPORTS ← EXTERNAL demand (foreign cycles) — can grow while domestic growth falls; net trade can offset/erase domestic weakness.
APPRECIATION → imports ↑, exports ↓, net exports ↓; DEPRECIATION the reverse.
FX matters only when CUMULATIVE in one direction over time; one-month/quarter moves ≈ minimal effect. GDP differentials = immediate; currency = gradual.

questions.front: Labor-force classification: employed, unemployed, underemployed, discouraged, voluntarily unemployed, frictional — in the labor force? counted as unemployed?
questions.back:
Employed (excl. informal sector): in LF, not unemployed.
Unemployed = actively seeking, no job: in LF, counted. Long-term (>3–4 months, still looking) and frictional (between jobs, new entrants) are both counted.
UNDEREMPLOYED (overqualified / part-time wanting full-time): has a job → EMPLOYED.
DISCOURAGED (stopped looking): OUTSIDE the labor force.
Voluntarily unemployed (refuses low wage, early retiree): outside LF.
Hidden unemployment = discouraged + underemployed.

questions.concept: UR and PR formulas + discouraged-worker effect
questions.front: Unemployment rate and participation rate formulas; what happens to each when discouraged workers leave / re-enter
questions.back:
Unemployment rate = Unemployed / LABOR FORCE (not population).
Participation rate = Labor force / WORKING-AGE population (16–64).
Example: LF 65, U 5, WA 100 → UR 7.69%, PR 65%.
1m give up → U 4 / LF 64 → UR 6.25% ↓, PR 64% ↓ (economy WORSE).
2m re-enter unhired → U 6 / LF 66 → UR 9.09% ↑, PR 66% ↑ (economy BETTER).
Always read UR together with PR.

questions.front: Two reasons unemployment is a lagging indicator, and the leading-to-lagging order of labor indicators
questions.back:
(1) The labor force expands/contracts with the economy — discouraged workers leave in bad times (rate looks better) and return in recoveries before finding jobs (rate looks worse). (2) Firms are reluctant to lay off and then fully use retained workers before rehiring.
Order: productivity (output/hours) → hours & overtime → TEMPORARY staff → full-time payrolls → unemployment rate.
Unemployment is highest somewhat AFTER recovery starts, lowest somewhat AFTER the peak.

questions.front: Laspeyres index formula (which quantities?), the Exhibit 3 numbers, and the three fixed-basket biases with their fixes
questions.back:
Index_t = Σ(q_BASE × p_t) / Σ(q_BASE × p_base) × 100 — base QUANTITIES, current PRICES (the GDP deflator is the reverse).
Exhibit 3: 458 → 515 → index 112.45 → inflation 12.45%.
Three biases, ALL UPWARD (S-Q-N): Substitution (fix: chained index), Quality (fix: hedonic pricing), New product (fix: add to basket).
Trigger word 'FIXED BASKET' → OVERSTATES cost of living. Bias = construction methodology, NOT which goods are included (headline vs core = noise, not bias).

questions.front: Deflation, disinflation, hyperinflation, stagflation, overheating — define each and say which can be read from the inflation rate alone
questions.back:
Deflation: sustained FALL in the price level (rate < 0).
Disinflation: inflation RATE falls but stays positive — prices still RISING.
Hyperinflation: extremely fast rise (500–1,000%/yr); cause = unbacked spending + money printing; cure = control the money supply.
Stagflation: high inflation + high unemployment/slow growth → left to self-correct. Needs TWO variables — NOT identifiable from the rate alone (deflation and hyperinflation are).
Overheating: high inflation + fast growth + low unemployment → policy cools it.

questions.front: Which data for cost-push vs demand-pull vs expectations; NAIRU definition, what it depends on, its TRUE limitations
questions.back:
COST-PUSH → UR vs NAIRU; wage growth vs productivity (ULC = W/O). Occurs when unemployment is LOW (below NAIRU) — never 'either'.
DEMAND-PULL → money growth vs nominal GDP; actual vs potential GDP; capacity utilization. Monetarist = MONEY GROWTH (not interest rates) = special case of demand-pull.
EXPECTATIONS → past trends; surveys; TIPS breakeven = nominal yield − TIPS yield.
NAIRU = NARU (Friedman): effective UR below which wage pressure emerges; depends on labor-force SKILL SET vs industrial mix. TRUE limitations: varies over time; misses segment bottlenecks; hard to observe. NOT a limitation: 'only in monetarist models'. NOT stems → T/F each option, pick the F.

questions.front: Velocity of money — formula and the four readings; money growth vs nominal GDP growth signals
questions.back:
Velocity = Nominal GDP / Money supply.
Stable → price stability. Falls via GDP ↓ (cyclical correction) → cyclical UPSWING likely, not inflation. Falls via MONEY ↑ → INFLATIONARY pressure. Rises → money shortage → disinflation/deflation. Always ask WHICH side moved.
Money growth > nominal GDP growth (esp. accelerating) → inflationary; money growth < economy (esp. decelerating) → disinflationary/deflationary.

questions.stem: A fall in a country's total imports is most likely the result of:

choices.B: a cyclical downturn among its primary trading partners
choices.C: a persistent depreciation of its currency against its trading partners

questions.explanation: Imports fall when domestic demand weakens or when foreign goods become relatively expensive. A depreciation makes foreign goods dearer → imports ↓ — and the stem says PERSISTENT, which is the condition for an FX move to affect trade at all. Faster domestic growth raises imports (A is the polarity flip); trading partners' cycles drive EXPORTS, not imports (B is the wrong side of the asymmetry).
questions.kr: 수입은 국내 수요 약화 또는 외국 재화 상대가격 상승 시 감소. 통화 약세 → 외국 재화 비싸짐 → 수입↓, 게다가 '지속적'이라 무역에 영향을 주는 조건 충족. 국내 성장 가속은 수입↑(A 극성 반대); 교역국 경기는 '수출'을 움직임(B).

questions.concept: UR and PR both fall → discouraged workers
questions.stem: A simultaneous decline in both the labor-force participation ratio and the unemployment rate is most likely explained by:

choices.A: a rise in the number of discouraged workers
choices.B: a rise in the number of underemployed workers
choices.C: a fall in the number of voluntarily unemployed persons

questions.explanation: Discouraged workers have stopped looking and are outside the labor force: the labor force shrinks → participation rate (LF / working-age pop) falls, and the unemployed count falls by the same people → unemployment rate falls. Underemployed workers are EMPLOYED, so they change neither ratio; fewer voluntarily unemployed means people re-entering the labor force → participation rate RISES.
questions.kr: 실망 실업자는 구직을 포기해 경제활동인구 밖 → 참가율↓, 실업자 수도 같이 줄어 실업률↓. 불완전고용자는 '취업자'라 두 비율에 영향 없음; 자발적 실업자 감소 = 경제활동인구 재진입 → 참가율↑.

questions.stem: A company's treasury manager has just resigned to take a better position at a rival firm that begins in six months. An employment survey taken today would most appropriately classify him as:

choices.C: frictionally unemployed

questions.explanation: Frictionally unemployed = between jobs, short-term and transitory: not working at survey time but has recently left one job and is about to start another. Having a job waiting does not remove him from the category — he simply hasn't started yet. Underemployed requires HAVING a job below one's qualifications; voluntarily unemployed means choosing to stay outside the labor force (refusing available work, early retirement).
questions.kr: 마찰적 실업 = 직장 사이의 단기·일시적 상태: 조사 시점에 일하지 않지만 곧 다음 직장을 시작. 자리가 정해져 있어도 아직 시작 전이면 마찰적 실업. 불완전고용은 자격 이하의 직장을 '가진' 경우; 자발적 실업은 스스로 노동시장 밖에 머무는 경우.

questions.stem: The discouraged-worker category consists of people who:

choices.A: hold a job for which they are overqualified
choices.B: are able to look for work but have chosen not to
choices.C: are actively looking for work but have not found it

questions.explanation: Discouraged workers have stopped looking for work and are outside the labor force. Overqualified job-holders are the UNDEREMPLOYED (counted as employed); people actively looking without success are the UNEMPLOYED (in the labor force).
questions.kr: 실망 실업자 = 구직을 포기해 경제활동인구 밖. 과잉자격 취업자는 불완전고용(취업자로 집계); 적극 구직 중 미취업자는 실업자(경제활동인구 안).

questions.stem: The group most likely to be hurt by a rise in the rate of inflation is:

choices.B: retirees living on a fixed annuity payment
choices.C: employees whose contracts contain wage escalator clauses

questions.explanation: Inflation erodes the purchasing power of FIXED nominal amounts — a fixed annuity buys fewer goods each year. Fixed-rate borrowers are protected (they repay with cheaper money); escalator clauses index wages to the CPI, so those workers are protected too. Mirror of the deflation logic: deflation hurts borrowers, inflation hurts fixed-income receivers and lenders.
questions.kr: 인플레이션은 '고정 명목 금액'의 구매력을 잠식 — 고정 연금은 매년 살 수 있는 양이 줄어듦. 고정금리 차입자는 보호(싸진 돈으로 상환), 물가연동(에스컬레이터) 조항 근로자도 보호. 디플레이션은 차입자, 인플레이션은 고정소득자·대출자가 손해.

questions.stem: The term for a situation in which the inflation rate falls but remains positive is:

choices.C: disinflation

questions.explanation: Disinflation = a reduction in the inflation rate from a higher to a lower, but still above-zero, level — the price level keeps rising, just more slowly. Deflation is a negative rate (falling price level); stagflation is high inflation together with stagnation/high unemployment.
questions.kr: 디스인플레이션 = 인플레이션율이 낮아지되 여전히 0 위 — 물가는 계속 오르는 중. 디플레이션은 음(−)의 상승률; 스태그플레이션은 높은 인플레이션 + 침체·고실업.

questions.stem: Deflation is most likely associated with:

choices.A: a shortfall in government tax revenue
choices.C: deliberate monetary policy aimed at reducing inflation

questions.explanation: Deflation is tied to a vicious cycle: falling prices → fixed nominal debts rise in real terms and revenues fall → firms cut spending, investment and jobs → less spending and higher unemployment → contraction deepens (US Great Depression, Japan since the late 1990s). Unbacked government spending is a cause of HYPERinflation; tightening to reduce inflation produces disinflation, not deflation.
questions.kr: 디플레이션은 악순환과 연결: 물가 하락 → 고정 명목부채의 실질부담↑·매출↓ → 기업의 지출·투자·고용 삭감 → 소비 감소·실업 증가 → 수축 심화(대공황, 1990년대 말 이후 일본). 세수 없는 재정지출은 '초인플레이션' 원인; 긴축은 디스인플레이션을 낳지 디플레이션이 아님.

questions.stem: Which of the following is least likely to accompany a period of hyperinflation?

choices.A: a decline in the velocity of money
choices.B: a rapid expansion of the money supply
choices.C: a heightened risk of social unrest

questions.explanation: LEAST-likely stem → mark each option T/F. Money-supply expansion is the CAUSE (T); social unrest / political risk is a documented consequence in developing economies (T). Velocity RISES in hyperinflation — people rush to convert cash into real goods, so money changes hands faster — so a decline in velocity is the F and the answer.
questions.kr: least likely 지문 → 선지별 T/F. 통화 공급 급증은 원인(T); 사회 불안·정치적 위험은 결과(T). 초인플레이션에서는 사람들이 현금을 실물로 바꾸려 해 유통속도가 '상승' → 유통속도 하락이 F = 정답.

questions.concept: Laspeyres index from a two-month basket
questions.stem: Base month: 70 kg of sugar at 0.90 and 60 kg of cotton at 0.60. Next month: 120 kg of sugar at 1.00 and 50 kg of cotton at 0.80. With the base-month index set at 100, the inflation rate implied by a Laspeyres index for the next month is closest to:
questions.explanation: Laspeyres holds BASE quantities (70, 60) fixed. Base bundle = 70×0.90 + 60×0.60 = 99. Same bundle at new prices = 70×1.00 + 60×0.80 = 118. Index = 118/99 × 100 = 119.19 → inflation 19.2%. Choice C (61.6%) is the change in total SPENDING (160/99) — quantities and prices both changed; choice B mixes new quantities into the base cost. Read which quantities are held fixed.
questions.kr: 라스파이레스 = 기준기 수량(70, 60) 고정. 기준 바스켓 99, 신가격 적용 118 → 지수 119.19 → 19.2%. C(61.6%)는 수량·가격이 모두 바뀐 총지출 변화(160/99); B는 기준 비용에 새 수량을 섞은 값.

questions.stem: Base month: 70 kg of sugar at 0.90 and 60 kg of cotton at 0.60. Next month: 120 kg of sugar at 1.00 and 50 kg of cotton at 0.80. The Paasche index for the next month (base = 100) is closest to:
questions.explanation: Paasche uses the CURRENT basket (120, 50) at both periods' prices: (120×1.00 + 50×0.80) / (120×0.90 + 50×0.60) = 160/138 × 100 = 115.9. Choice C (160) is just current spending with no base-cost denominator; choice B (148 ≈ 160/108) uses a wrong base. Laspeyres = base quantities; Paasche = current quantities (the GDP-deflator convention).
questions.kr: 파셰 = '현재' 수량(120, 50)을 양 기간 가격에 적용: 160/138 × 100 = 115.9. C(160)는 분모 없는 현재 지출; B는 잘못된 기준 비용. 라스파이레스 = 기준 수량, 파셰 = 현재 수량(GDP 디플레이터 방식).

questions.stem: A central bank is most likely to let the economy correct itself, rather than intervene, during a period of:

choices.A: high inflation, fast growth and low unemployment
choices.B: low inflation, slow growth and high unemployment
choices.C: high inflation, slow growth and high unemployment

questions.explanation: High inflation + slow growth + high unemployment = STAGFLATION, which is left to self-correct because no short-term policy is thought effective (tightening worsens the slump; easing worsens inflation). Choice A is OVERHEATING, where policy moves to cool the economy — the other row of the same table. Choice B is an ordinary recession, where easing is the standard response. Two-row mapping: overheating → act; stagflation → wait.
questions.kr: 고인플레 + 저성장 + 고실업 = 스태그플레이션 → 단기 정책이 효과 없다고 보아 자율 조정에 맡김(긴축은 침체 악화, 완화는 인플레 악화). A는 과열 → 정책으로 식힘. B는 일반 침체 → 완화 정책. 두 행의 매핑: 과열 → 개입, 스태그플레이션 → 방치.

questions.stem: Disinflation is best described as:

choices.A: a decline in the price level
choices.C: a decline in the inflation rate

questions.explanation: Disinflation = the inflation RATE falls (e.g., 7% → 4%) while staying positive — the price level keeps rising. Choices A and B both describe DEFLATION (falling price level = negative rate). Level vs rate of change.
questions.kr: 디스인플레이션 = 인플레이션'율'이 하락(7% → 4%)하되 양수 유지 — 물가는 계속 상승. A·B는 모두 디플레이션(물가 수준 하락 = 음의 상승률). 수준 vs 변화율.

questions.concept: CPI — what is shared across countries
questions.stem: Across major economies, the feature national consumer price indexes most likely have in common is:

choices.A: the geographic coverage of their surveys
choices.B: the weights assigned to the goods and services covered
choices.C: their use in setting macroeconomic policy

questions.explanation: Central banks everywhere use a CPI to monitor inflation and judge monetary policy. Coverage differs (US CPI-U is urban-only; China and Germany survey urban + rural) and weights differ sharply (food ≈ 14–15% in Germany/US vs 30–47% in China/India). The shared element is the USE, not the construction.
questions.kr: 모든 중앙은행이 CPI로 인플레이션을 감시하고 통화정책을 평가. 조사 범위(미국 CPI-U는 도시만)와 가중치(식품 비중 14~47%)는 나라마다 크게 다름. 공통점은 '구성'이 아니라 '용도'.

questions.stem: Which statement about the producer price index (PPI) is least likely to be accurate? The PPI:

choices.B: has category weights that vary more across countries than CPI weights do
choices.C: is used more often than the CPI to adjust labor-contract payments

questions.explanation: LEAST-likely stem → T/F each option. A is TRUE: producer price rises pass through to consumers, so PPI leads CPI. B is TRUE: cross-country PPI weight differences are 'much more dramatic' (industry specialization). C is FALSE: labor contracts and leases are indexed to the CPI; the PPI (and its sub-indexes) is linked to BUSINESS contracts. In a NOT question the true statements are the distractors.
questions.kr: least likely → 선지별 T/F. A 참(생산자 가격이 소비자에게 전가 → PPI가 CPI를 선행). B 참(국가 간 PPI 가중치 차이는 CPI보다 훨씬 큼). C 거짓: 노동계약·임대차는 CPI에 연동, PPI는 '기업 간 계약'에 연동. NOT 문제에서 참인 문장은 오답.

questions.concept: Which index gives the highest inflation (Laspeyres vs Paasche vs Fisher)
questions.stem: Base month: 18 liters of milk at 1.00 and 6 liters of juice at 2.00. Next month: 17 liters of milk at 1.00 and 4 liters of juice at 2.50. Over the two months, the highest inflation rate is produced by a price index that uses:

choices.C: a basket reflecting consumers' substitutions over time

questions.explanation: Constant basket = Laspeyres: base cost 18×1 + 6×2 = 30; at new prices 18×1 + 6×2.5 = 33 → 110 → 10%. Current basket = Paasche: (17×1 + 4×2.5)/(17×1 + 4×2) = 27/25 → 108 → 8%. Fisher (substitution-adjusted) = √(110 × 108) = 108.99 → 8.99%. Laspeyres is HIGHEST because the fixed basket ignores the shift away from the good that got dearer (juice) — the substitution bias in action. Rule: Laspeyres overstates → highest; Paasche lowest; Fisher between.
questions.kr: 고정 바스켓(라스파이레스): 30 → 33 → 10%. 현재 바스켓(파셰): 27/25 → 8%. 피셔(대체 반영) = √(110×108) = 108.99 → 8.99%. 라스파이레스가 가장 높은 이유 = 비싸진 재화(주스)에서 이탈하는 대체를 무시(대체 편의). 규칙: 라스파이레스 과대 → 최고, 파셰 최저, 피셔 중간.

questions.stem: The inflation measure most likely relied upon when setting public economic policy is:

choices.C: an index of food and energy prices

questions.explanation: Policy makers read the trend through CORE inflation (headline minus food and energy) because it is less volatile and less likely to provoke policy overreactions to short-term swings. Headline is the full but noisy measure. 'An index of food and energy prices' is not a concept the curriculum uses at all — the off-model lure built from the words of the core definition.
questions.kr: 정책 당국은 '근원' 인플레이션(헤드라인 − 식품·에너지)으로 추세를 읽음 — 변동성이 낮아 단기 변동에 과잉반응할 위험이 적음. 헤드라인은 전체 지표지만 노이즈가 큼. '식품·에너지 지수'는 교재에 없는 개념 — 근원 정의의 단어로 만든 유인 선지.

questions.stem: In a cost-push inflation setting, the most important role of labor productivity is that:

choices.A: rising productivity signals a strong economy and therefore an inflationary bias
choices.B: the productivity level fixes where unemployment sits relative to its natural rate
choices.C: when productivity growth outpaces wage growth, price increases become less likely

questions.explanation: ULC = W / O: the faster output per hour grows, the further wages can rise without raising cost per unit of output — so productivity growth exceeding wage growth REMOVES cost pressure. Choice A has the sign backwards (productivity is disinflationary); choice B confuses productivity with NAIRU, which depends on the labor force's skill mix.
questions.kr: ULC = W / O: 시간당 산출이 빨리 늘수록 단위비용 상승 없이 임금이 더 오를 수 있음 → 생산성 증가율 > 임금 증가율이면 가격 압력 감소. A는 부호 반대(생산성은 디스인플레이션 요인), B는 NAIRU(노동력 숙련 구성)와 혼동.

questions.concept: Quality bias — price constant, quality up
questions.stem: A good in a fixed-basket price index improves in quality over time while its price is unchanged. The measured inflation rate is most likely:

choices.C: biased downward

questions.explanation: Quality bias: a better product at the same price is a REAL price fall per unit of quality, but the fixed-basket index records no change — so measured inflation is HIGHER than true inflation → biased upward (the index overstates). It would still bias upward if the price had risen. Fix = hedonic adjustment. 'Unaffected' is the lure: no price change ≠ no bias. Trigger word: fixed basket → S-Q-N, all upward.
questions.kr: 품질 편의: 같은 가격에 더 좋은 제품 = 품질 단위당 실질 가격 하락인데 고정 바스켓 지수는 변화 없음으로 기록 → 측정 인플레이션이 실제보다 높음 → 상향 편의. 가격이 올랐어도 마찬가지. 해결 = 헤도닉 조정. '영향 없음'이 유인: 가격 불변 ≠ 편의 없음. 트리거: fixed basket → S-Q-N 모두 상향.

questions.stem: A price index that excludes food and energy is most likely used to calculate:

choices.C: headline inflation

questions.explanation: Core = all items EXCEPT food and energy; headline = ALL items; GDP deflator = prices of domestic output (not a consumption basket at all). Policy makers use core to read the trend without overreacting to short-term food/energy swings. This is the same fact as the 'policy relies on core' item — missed twice in one set → flashcard until automatic.
questions.kr: 근원 = 식품·에너지 '제외'; 헤드라인 = 전 품목; GDP 디플레이터 = 국내 산출물 가격(소비 바스켓 아님). 정책 당국은 단기 변동에 과잉반응하지 않으려 근원을 사용. 같은 세트에서 두 번 틀린 사실 → 자동화될 때까지 플래시카드.

questions.concept: Cost-push vs demand-pull from a two-step story
questions.stem: An economist expects that falling unemployment will lift home-retailer revenues, and that a tighter labor market will push wages up, forcing those retailers to raise prices. The economist's expectations best describe:

choices.C: demand-pull inflation

questions.explanation: Read the WHOLE stem: the mechanism that produces the price rise is 'rising wages compel firms to raise prices' — the literal definition of cost-push. The first clause (unemployment ↓ → revenues ↑) is demand-side scenery that lures you to demand-pull; demand-pull would be 'rising demand raises prices, THEN workers chase wages'. The order of the chain decides: costs → prices = cost-push; demand → prices → wages = demand-pull. Stagflation needs high unemployment, the opposite of the stem.
questions.kr: 지문 전체를 읽는다: 가격 상승의 메커니즘은 '임금 상승이 기업을 가격 인상으로 몬다' — cost-push의 정의 그대로. 첫 문장(실업↓ → 매출↑)은 수요 쪽 배경일 뿐 demand-pull 유인. 사슬의 순서가 결정: 비용 → 가격 = cost-push; 수요 → 가격 → 임금 = demand-pull. 스태그플레이션은 고실업이 필요(지문과 반대).

questions.front: Headline vs. core inflation — one sentence that resolves every version of the question (missed 3×)
questions.back:
CORE = HEADLINE MINUS food and energy; policy makers rely on CORE because it is less volatile and avoids overreaction to short-term swings.
→ 'excludes food & energy' = core. 'used for policy' = core. 'all items' = headline. Headline vs core = more NOISE, never 'bias' (bias comes from the fixed-basket construction and applies to both). 'An index of food and energy prices' is not a curriculum concept.

questions.front: Which index gives the highest inflation and why; Fisher formula; which index adjusts which contract
questions.back:
Laspeyres (base basket) OVERSTATES → highest. Paasche (current basket) understates → lowest. Fisher = √(I_L × I_P) → between. Milk/juice example: 10% > 8.99% > 8%. Reason: the fixed basket ignores substitution away from the good that got dearer.
Quality bias: better product at SAME price → measured inflation biased UPWARD (not 'unaffected').
Indexation: TIPS ← CPI-U; labor contracts & leases ← CPI; business contracts ← PPI. PPI leads CPI (pass-through) and its weights differ more across countries.
